We have been wanting to go to TopGolf in Ft. Worth for several years now. We knew about it because we would often drive by it on the freeway on the way to certain places, like malls, the airport, etc. We did a little investigating online in the past to find out more about it. With family visiting us for the Fourth of July, it finally worked out right to go for the first time. The only issue that I had is when I tried to make a reservation online earlier in the week. It was the same-day, but it didn't make it clear whether the reservation went through or not. However, it did say "Just come on down, we gladly take walk-ins." So, we did. When we got there, they said that it was a 2 1/2 hour wait for walk-ins and reservations were recommended. We life around 20 miles away, so I wish they would've made it more clear online. We were unable to wait the 2 1/2 hours and had to leave. Later on, I was able to make a reservation online, but the first available was on the Fourth. When that reservation went through, I then understood how that works. I wish I would've understood it better the first time around when we went down there. With all that being said, once we got there on the Fourth, we were very pleased with everything. It was a really hot day, but that was the only difficulty. We learned our way through how to take advantage of all that was offered to us. We originally booked for 1 hour to start and ended up staying for 2 hours. The food was very good, the drinks were always cold and very helpful with the heat, and the service was very attentive and friendly. Also, the environment was very clean, contemporary, and efficient in the layout of everything. With our scheduling, I don't know for sure when we can make it back, but we definitely will be back.

My drink was also made incorrectly twice. Again, I don’t necessarily blame the server because he seemed to be doing the best he could under difficult circumstances.

Another surprise was the price. We usually visit on half-price nights, so we were caught off guard when this visit ended up costing about twice what we normally spend. Topgolf is already a fairly expensive outing, so combined with everything else that happened, it made the experience feel even more disappointing.

Overall, we left feeling really let down. We genuinely enjoy coming to this location, which is why this experience stood out so much. Because we visit so often, I expected a much better experience than what we had, and honestly, it’s made me hesitant to come back for a while.

I was given two e-gift cards. The first I used at The Colony location and the second I wanted to use at my home location in San Antonio but the team member went to go speak with his manager about using the gift card and ended up just charging my card for the full price. He mentioned he wasn't sure on how to apply the gift card before he left. With today's technology and the tech y'all have at every Topgolf location, it's not the best user experience y'all have in place for someone to use an e-gift card. The email I received pertaining to the gift cards mentioned printing and allowing the team member write down the e-card numbers. I took screen shots (on my phone) of the e-cards thinking y'all could scan the bar code but that wasn't the case. At The Colony location, your team member had to write down the gift card numbers then head back to her monitor in order to apply the gift card to the transaction. And my recent trip (San Antonio) the team member didn't even try. Aside from that, I would be curious to know how many people actually print out their gift cards, and what percentage of people are purchasing gift cards. We're at the moment in time where tech has greatly improved the user experience, and while you have that on the gaming side, you're lacking at the very end when it's time to pay. I can go inside grocery stores and pay via my iPhone, I can go to a sporting event or movie theater and have my digital ticket directly on my phone, or I can add a gift card to my Chick-Fil-A account and have it easily accessible in my payment options. But I have to print out or have one of your Top Golf members write down the gift card numbers in order to apply it to my bill. Now for the ideas on how to improve your user experiences. I have your TopGolf app and users should be allowed to add their gift cards to their digital accounts. When it's time to pay, a user should be able to tap/click on a gift card within your app and a TopGolf member could scan it and apply payment right from the bay. This is assuming you upgrade and have hand-held devices that are capable of going to each bay and conducting the transaction in front of the customer. Another idea is creating the e-gift card to be able to apply to digital wallets, like the iPhone. I could click on my gift card within my digital wallet, and a TopGolf associate could scan it at their POS system. This method would end up with the customer giving up their phone so the associate could scan it. But again, a hand-held device with capabilities of payment and scanning would help right from within each bay. I really hope y'all can improve the gift card method.

As longtime service industry employees, both my date and IO know what great customer service looks like, as well as poor customer service.  Last night, we experienced both at this location.

So, we were mystified when we sat for 10 minutes, utterly ignored by staff.  They congregated in a group at the server station, laughing and chatting with each other, and texting on their phones.  (I snapped several pics of their conclave.)  None made any effort to acknowledge us, or the other four customers who were sitting at the bar.  

After 10 minutes, I walked over to them and asked the first person whose attention I grabbed, whose name was Connor, if there was any way I could bother him to take a drink order.  I also asked him directly why nobody had acknowledged us?  Connor ignored the question, but asked how he could help?  I repeated that we simply wanted to order drinks.  Connor complied, and proceeded to pour us two draft beers, bringing them to us totally flat, in warm glasses with no heads.  We asked Connor about ordering food.  He stated that he could not take a food order, but he would "get someone else to help us".  Connor then disappeared.  We were utterly shocked with his apathetic attitude, and his utter unwillingness to even make eye contact, let alone engage and make us feel comfortable.  

After a further ten minutes, I again walked to the server station where 4-5 associates were still congregating, and asked Emma for assistance.  Emma took our food order and poured us two more beers, which came in frosted mugs with perfect heads.  Yay!!

During our ninety minutes at the bar, other associates (in red and blue shirts) walked past the bar and engaged with bar staff, but made no effort to break up the congregation at the server station.  I also observed at least one additional bar customer who was forced to get up and walk to the server station simply to gain staff's attention.

Fortunately, when we moved to our Bay 323 for golf, things improved markedly.  Our server, Piper, was smiling, engaging, helpful and FAST.  She helped with drinks, pizza and silverware, and could not have been more helpful.  Well done, Piper! 

At 8pm, we finished golf and returned to the bar for one last drink and to watch the finish of the baseball game.  At this time, the bar was far more busy.  

Staff walked by us at least a dozen times before we once again asked to be acknowledged.  My date ordered a Margarita, and found it to be mixed far too sweet.  We once again attempted to gain someone's attention to address her concern, and after 10 minutes, we decided it wasn't worth the fight.  So, we decided to pay the tab and leave.  

Emma walked by, and we asked her to cash us out.  She indicated that she would "get someone to help us" and walked back to the Server station. I’m writing to share feedback regarding a frustrating and disappointing experience during our recent visit to Topgolf. What was meant to be a fun Father’s Day celebration for my husband and our children turned into an afternoon of miscommunication, inflexibility, and questionable service — particularly in our interactions with management.

We had booked a 2-hour reservation in advance. Upon arrival, we were placed in a ground-floor bay at the far end, where our children were unable to hit balls toward any targets. While I understand that specific bay reservations aren’t possible, I believe flexibility and a reasonable process for requesting a more accessible bay should be an allowable consideration. Who would want to spend $200 for a bay that our children literally couldn’t hit a target out of - that is the whole purpose in being there.

When we politely asked to be moved, we were met with a robotic and dismissive response: “All bays are full; there’s a three-hour wait; it’s our busiest day of the year; nothing can be done.” When we asked to speak with a manager, we received the same answer, with the only “solution” being to join a waitlist that might take several hours. Even after explaining that we were open to waiting a reasonable amount of time, there was no willingness to help. The manager said he would add us to a “priority” list, though he emphasized it could still be 2–3 hours. We had a reservation - we shouldn’t have to go at the end of a waitlist simply for the next open bay. 

After nearly 20 minutes of trying to compromise on a solution with the manager we agreed to go on the “priority” wait list that could take 2-3 hours, and we went to play pool. Then suddenly, as soon as we got downstairs to start playing pool - a bay was ready for us within 3–4 minutes. This sudden change, after being told repeatedly that nothing could be done, was deeply frustrating and suggested a lack of transparency in the process.

Unfortunately, the issues didn’t end there. Once we arrived at our bay, we encountered a problem with the reservation time. Though we had booked for two hours, the system would only allow us one. When we flagged this to our server, the floor manager came over and stated that due to how busy it was, we would only get one hour. He later added that there was a “party reservation” scheduled in our bay — a completely different explanation that simply didn’t add up.

When I pointed out that we had a confirmed 2-hour reservation and asked to be moved if necessary, the manager left, returned, and suddenly informed us that the “party” had been moved, and we could stay for our full reservation. Again, this lack of consistency — and what felt like outright dishonesty — was incredibly frustrating.

As someone who has worked at Topgolf before, I know the standards you strive for in terms of hospitality, guest experience, and integrity. What we experienced was far from that. We were not treated as valued guests. It’s unfortunate that a place that should be known for fun and service left us hurdling obstacles and feeling misled and unappreciated on a day that was meant to be special for our family.

There are many entertainment options out there now. Experiences like this are exactly what drive loyal customers away. I hope you’ll take this feedback seriously and revisit how your teams handle guest concerns and reservations — particularly on high-traffic days.
